chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

He said to me: “If you were to perform wudu (ablution), and you made the wiping of the feet into washing, then inwardly held that this was among what is obligatory, that would not be wudu (ablution).”
Then he said: “Begin with wiping over the feet. Then if it occurs to you to wash, and you wash them, then wipe after that so that the last of that may be the obligatory act.”

key_terms.مَسْحَ: wiping, the prescribed act over the feet in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, is washing the feet sufficient in wudu (ablution), or must they be wiped?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a ruling of wudu (ablution) concerning the feet: the obligatory act is wiping, not washing as a substitute for wiping. It also states that if washing occurs, wiping must still come afterward so that the prescribed obligatory act is fulfilled correctly.
